records.title: Foundations of Proactive Agents: Principles, Technical Layers, and Proactivity-Gym

records.title: JevAgentHarness: Benchmarking, Deploying and Training Decision Models That Share Control with LLMs

records.title: Evolving to Match Capabilities: Improving Harness Self-Evolution via Skill Adaptation
records.summary: Harness self-evolution improves LLM agents via skill adaptation guided by a meta-skill that reformulates guidance to match executor capabilities, boosting weak models without parameter updates.

records.title: Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit: Disentangling Evolution Capabilities in Self-Evolving LLM Agents
records.summary: Research reveals that harness self-evolution capabilities in LLM agents show unexpected patterns: harness-updating effectiveness is consistent across model capabilities, while harness-benefit follows a non-monotonic trend with mid-tier models performing best.

records.title: The Next Challenge for Agentic Cybersecurity: A Realistic, Contamination-Free Reverse Engineering Benchmark

records.title: Cultivar: A Contrastive and Locale-Oriented Translation Benchmark for Investigating Contamination and Localisation Robustness

records.summary: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as general-purpose conversational assistants, they must handle diverse user requests while reliably refusing harmful ones. records.summary: Peer-review comments check what a paper does and judge why it matters, but no existing scheme distinguishes these two evaluative acts. records.title: JEV-as-a-Judge: Accept When Confident, Escalate When Unsure
records.summary: A decision-only judge offers a low-cost first evaluation pass that closely matches stronger judges on common tasks, with a frozen cascade preserving nearly all accuracy by escalating only uncertain cases.

records.summary: AgentJudgeBench reveals that LLM judges face structural reliability limits on dependency-driven agentic tool-calling workflows, with alignment degrading by difficulty and ground-truth exposure yielding mixed effects.

records.summary: A benchmark generator called RankJudge evaluates large language model judges on multi-turn conversations by creating flawed conversation pairs and using statistical models for ranking and difficulty assessment.

records.title: IndicBankBench: Evaluating Safety and Reliability of Language Model Assistants in Indian Retail Banking
records.summary: IndicBankBench evaluates Indian banking assistants across 799 cases with multi-stage checks, revealing that strict reliability is substantially lower than at-least-once success.

records.title: Codifying the Judge: Scalable Evaluation via Program Distillation
records.summary: Program distillation replaces LLM judges with transparent, efficient programmatic evaluators that match performance while reducing cost and latency.

records.title: EduPanel: A Three-Agent LLM Judge for Teaching Videos -- Reliability, Complementarity, and Human Trust Calibration
records.summary: EduPanel is a rubric-based, learner-conditioned LLM judge that evaluates teaching video quality through specialized agents, achieving expert-level reliability while assisting rather than replacing human evaluators.

records.title: Mitigating Perceptual Judgment Bias in Multimodal LLM-as-a-Judge via Perceptual Perturbation and Reward Modeling
records.summary: Researchers identify a perceptual judgment bias in multimodal large language models where visual evidence is overlooked for textual plausibility, and propose a training framework using a perturbed dataset and reward modeling to improve perceptual fidelity and evaluation consistency.

records.title: MÖVE: A Holistic LLM Benchmark for the German Public Sector
records.summary: A comprehensive benchmark for evaluating large language models in German public sector applications, assessing both performance and governance criteria across multiple German-language datasets.

records.title: Binarization Flattens the Score Space
records.summary: Using graded rather than binary LLM judge scores reveals hidden policy changes and reduces ambiguity, though some improvements remain indistinguishable from sycophancy without external validation.

records.title: Jagged Judges: Epistemic Stability Under Silence, Pressure, and Persistence
records.summary: The Wiggle Framework evaluates LLM judge stability across mechanical consistency, single-turn conviction, and multi-turn persistence, revealing high verdict-flipping rates under challenge and identifying jury majority strength as a predictive signal.

records.title: LLM Judges Verify Presence, Not Absence: Omission Blindness in AI Clinical Notes and What Recovers It
records.summary: A structured fact-listing approach enables LLM judges to detect omitted clinical information more reliably than direct comparison, though restated facts remain challenging.

records.title: Historical Backtesting for Scientific Question Discovery: A Protocol and Astronomy Pilot
records.summary: Historical backtesting evaluates scientific question generators by comparing frozen past questions against future literature, revealing that evidence-based generation outperforms LLM prompting and that judge agreement metrics overstate reliability.

records.title: Compaction as Epistemic Failure: How Agentic LLM Tools Fabricate Confirmed Results from Killed Processes
records.summary: Agentic coding tools can propagate false results across sessions by treating partial terminal output from failed commands as verified outcomes in compaction summaries.

records.title: Can LLM-as-a-Judge Reliably Verify Rubrics in Agentic Scenarios?
records.summary: LLM-as-a-Judge reliability for rubric scoring in agentic scenarios is systematically evaluated through a new benchmark, revealing significant noise even in advanced models and identifying effective strategies for improving verification accuracy.

records.title: Metric Match: A Subset Selection Approach to Evaluating LLM Judge Reliability
records.summary: A method called Metric Match is developed to estimate the reliability of LLM judges using limited human annotations by selecting representative sample subsets that match population reliability metrics, demonstrating superior performance over random selection in terms of estimation accuracy and reduced annotation costs.
